MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fundamentals of Aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Fundamentals of Aquaculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fundamentals of Aquaculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fundamentals of Aquaculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fundamentals of Aquaculture.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fundamentals of Marine and freshwater fisheries Technology 1.2 Fish morphology a? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fundamentals of Marine and freshwater fisheries Technology 1.2 Fish morphology a.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fundamentals of Marine and freshwater fisheries Technology 1.2 Fish morphology a.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fundamentals of Marine and freshwater fisheries Technology 1.2 Fish morphology a.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fundamentals of Marine and freshwater fisheries Technology 1.2 Fish morphology a.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Morphology and Anatomy? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Morphology and Anatomy.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Morphology and Anatomy.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Morphology and Anatomy.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Morphology and Anatomy.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fundamentals of capture fisheries 3.2 Safety and Survival Techniques Page 15 of ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fundamentals of capture fisheries 3.2 Safety and Survival Techniques Page 15 of .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fundamentals of capture fisheries 3.2 Safety and Survival Techniques Page 15 of .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fundamentals of capture fisheries 3.2 Safety and Survival Techniques Page 15 of .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fundamentals of capture fisheries 3.2 Safety and Survival Techniques Page 15 of .

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Production Systems? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Production Systems.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Production Systems.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Production Systems.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Production Systems.
